Every item in a list or a pair must have the same form. All ing words, all plain verbs, all nouns, or all describing words.
Think of a row of matching dominoes. If one is a different shape, the whole row breaks.
Here's the method. Find the other items in the list. Look at their form. Then make the blank match.
The researchers spent their days measuring, photographing, and blank the coral. Measuring, photographing: both ing words. So the answer is sampling.
Trap alert. To sample switches to a to plus verb form. It breaks the ing pattern.
One to can cover a whole list. The guide told the hikers to stretch, drink water, and rest. Stretch, drink, rest. All plain verbs.
Things in a list stay things. The experiment needed soil, seeds, and a light source. Lighting the plants would be an action in a list of things.
Pairs count too. Not only, but also. Both, and. Either, or. Whatever follows the first part must match whatever follows the second.
Let's try an SAT style question. The new library is not only larger but also blank. Quieter, or it is quieter?
Not only larger. But also quieter. Larger and quieter are both describing words. They match.
Trap alert. It is quieter adds a whole new sentence part. It doesn't match larger.
Your turn. Pause the video. She enjoys hiking, swimming, and blank. To read, or reading?
Reading. Hiking, swimming, reading. All ing words.
Remember three things. Find the other items. Check their form. And make the blank match. Great work.
